plan_a_advantages: Dedicated strength and mobility work to improve power and injury resistance.
Longer, more substantial long runs (102 and 127 minutes) for endurance building.
Strategic placement of tempo runs to develop threshold strength.
plan_b_advantages: More frequent trail running sessions, potentially leading to better adaptation to trail conditions.
Includes interval training, which can be effective for improving speed and efficiency (though not as targeted as Plan A’s tempo runs).
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates dedicated strength and mobility work alongside longer, more challenging runs. While Plan B focuses heavily on aerobic development and hill work, it lacks a crucial element for trail running speed – the ability to generate power and maintain efficiency over longer distances. Plan A’s inclusion of a strength session directly addresses this, building the foundational strength needed to handle the demands of trail terrain. Furthermore, the slightly longer duration of the long runs in Plan A (102 and 127 minutes) provides a greater opportunity for the athlete to build endurance at a sustainable pace, which is vital for faster times.
